quotationPolicy: Short paraphrases only; no paper figures, reference photos or videos copied or used as image-model inputs

sources.title: How the hummingbird wingbeat is tuned for efficient hovering
sources.scope: Six male Anna's hummingbirds trained to hover at a stationary feeder; high-speed kinematics and aerodynamic force measurements
observations: Weight support occurs during both strokes and is unequal
Direction reversal of the wing is a mechanically important part of the cycle
sources.productionInference: Draw actual returning wings as well as power-stroke wings; keep wing phase separate from root trajectory
sources.caveat: No universal wingbeat frequency, exact duty ratio or game timing is inferred; no take-off or landing measurements claimed
sources.licenseStatus: Publisher displays a user-license link; exact reusable-media terms not verified here. Facts-only use; no media downloaded

sources.title: Backward flight in hummingbirds employs unique kinematic adjustments and entails low metabolic cost
sources.scope: Five male Anna's hummingbirds, wind-tunnel feeding, forward/backward/hover comparisons; one individual's extended speed range
observations: Reverse flight differs in body inclination, head flexion and stroke-plane orientation
Head flexion helps retain a near-horizontal bill despite a steeper body
Approach, hover feeding and backward retreat are described as the typical flower visit sequence
Small bill movements were observed; birds were not obviously hanging by the bill
sources.productionInference: Use an upright reverse pose with compensating head angle; flower/bill alignment is not a support joint
sources.caveat: Laboratory sustained reverse flight is not a direct measurement of a short garden brake or perch landing
sources.licenseStatus: No CC/PD media license verified; facts-only use; no paper media downloaded

sources.title: Take-off mechanics in hummingbirds (Trochilidae)
sources.scope: Rufous hummingbird, Selasphorus rufus; instrumented perch and high-speed video
observations: Wings beat while the hindlimbs are still providing thrust
sources.productionInference: Comparative reason to propose wing activation before toe release rather than folded-wing airborne translation
sources.caveat: Not Anna-specific. No rufous numerical force contributions, wingbeat rate or exact timing transferred to Anna
sources.licenseStatus: Publisher copyright; facts-only use; no media downloaded
